For the Appellant/s : Mr.Mukesh Kumar Rana, Adv.
 For the Respondent/s : Mrs. Anita Kumari Singh, App

= = = =
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJIV ROY  ORAL ORDER 6 10-02-2025 Heard Mr. Mukesh Kumar Rana, learned counsel for the appellant and Mrs. Anita Kumari Singh.

2. The present memo of appeal has been filed for the following reliefs:-
"That, this memo of appeal is directed against the Judgment of conviction dated 14.12.2023, and order of sentence dated 18.12.2023, passed by Sri Ajay Kumar -1,
Learned Additional Sessions Judge VI, cum Special Judge POCSO Court, Araria, in Special (POCSO) Case No. 12 of 2020, arising out of Araria (Mahila) No. 36 of 2020,
whereby and where under this appellant has been convicted for the following offences:-
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.669 of 2024(6) dt.10-02-2025 Fine of Rs.
50,000/- Further SI Under Section Under of 3 months in case of default Section 376 of I.P.C. and R.l. for 10 years section 4 of POCSO Act 3.
Earlier the case stands admitted on 04.04.2024 and the trial court record was called for which has been received now.

4. Today the matter has come up for bail and learned counsel for the appellant submits that he is in custody since 15.05.2020 (para 16).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned APP opposes the prayer submitting that the allegation against him is heinous, he has not completed even half of his jail term, in that background, he does not deserve bail.

6. This Court has also perused the trial court record as also the allegation that has come/proved, as rightly pointed out by the learned APP that he has not even completed half of his term, in that background, there is no need to take a look on his bail.

(Rajiv Roy, J)
